args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest production deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1, the service failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. I rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is down to about 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and find out why it was promoted even though its release candidate was unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Before:** v2.3.1 was running in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and failing health checks, with an error rate of about 18%.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so all three regions now run it. A status check afterward shows the service is healthy and the error rate is down to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** It records the failure, the rollback and the recovery. It also asks for follow-up on two things: what caused v2.3.1 to fail, and why it was released even though its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had already failed health checks in staging.
